title: Reverse-Sear Steak with Chimichurri
summary: Your low-oven reverse sear: edge-to-edge medium-rare, a 75-second crust and zingy RecipeTin chimichurri.
profile: Beef-forward and savory: the all-purpose steak seasoning brings the salt (about 1% on the meat) and a peppery, garlicky backbone, the hard sear adds deep roasted notes, and the chimichurri cuts the richness with sharp red wine vinegar, raw garlic, grassy parsley and optional chili heat. Texture target: evenly pink medium-rare from edge to edge (about 125–130°F in the center after the sear) with almost no gray band, under a thin, dark, crisp crust; the chimichurri is finely chopped and loose, never a puree. Delivers 2 servings per pound of steak in about 1¼ hours, mostly hands-off oven time, plus ¾ cup chimichurri (more than a pound of steak needs); serve sliced against the grain with the sauce spooned over or alongside. Sliced leftover steak keeps 3 days refrigerated; eat it cold or warm it gently in a 250°F (120°C) oven so it stays pink, and keep the chimichurri airtight in the fridge for up to 3 days.

source.author: Your method; chimichurri from RecipeTin Eats (Nagi Maehashi)

yield: 1 lb steak + about ¾ cup chimichurri
equipment: wire rack set in a rimmed sheet pan

ingredients.note: table salt; or 1 tsp Diamond Crystal / a heaping ½ tsp Morton kosher
cut not specified in your notes (ribeye, NY strip or sirloin all work); reverse sear wants a thick steak, about 1¼–2 inches
your "multi" seasoning, 1 tbsp per pound of steak; assumes a salted blend (if yours is salt-free, add 1½ tsp Diamond Crystal per lb)
high smoke point (avocado, canola), for the sear

steps.text: Put the parsley, oregano, garlic, red pepper flakes, vinegar, salt and a few grinds of pepper in a food processor and pulse until the parsley is finely chopped but not pureed (or chop everything by hand). Transfer to a small bowl and gently stir in the olive oil. Let it stand at least 1 hour before serving (overnight is even better), so make it before the steak goes in.
steps.tip: The hour lets the vinegar tame the raw garlic and the herbs flavor the oil.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 250°F (120°C) with a rack in the middle. Pat the steak dry and season it all over, edges included, with the seasoning (1 tbsp per pound). Set it on a wire rack over a rimmed sheet pan.
steps.tip: Season right before it goes in or at least 40 minutes ahead (up to a day, uncovered in the fridge); in between, the drawn-out brine sits on the surface and fights the crust.

steps.text: Roast until an instant-read thermometer in the center of the thickest part reads 100°F, 20–50 minutes depending on thickness (start checking at 20 minutes for a 1¼-inch steak).
steps.tip: The low oven cooks the steak evenly edge to edge, so there's almost no gray band under the crust.

steps.text: Take the steak out, still on the rack, and let it rest uncovered until the center coasts up to about 115°F, 10–15 minutes. Meanwhile, heat the skillet over medium-high heat for a few minutes, then add the oil; it's ready when the oil shimmers and just starts to smoke.
steps.tip: Leave it uncovered: foil traps steam and softens the dry surface you want for the sear.

steps.text: Sear the steak 75 seconds per wide side over medium-high heat, without moving it, until deeply browned; flip once. The center should finish around 125–130°F, medium-rare.
steps.tip: The oven already dried the surface, so a short, hot sear builds the crust without overcooking the pink layer underneath.

steps.text: Slice the steak against the grain right away (it rested before the sear, so it won't bleed much) and serve with the chimichurri spooned over or on the side.

changelog.summary: Built from your Recipe List notes (Reverse Sear steak) with the chimichurri from RecipeTin Eats. Kept your numbers (1 tbsp seasoning per lb, 250°F oven, pull at 100°F, rest to ~115°F, 75 s per wide side over medium-high); added pat-dry, rack over a sheet pan, thermometer, sear oil and slicing against the grain. Steak cut wasn't specified; the chimichurri's plain "salt" is read as table salt.
